question: Can normalization statistics computed over the hidden units of a single training case, instead of over a mini-batch, speed up training and work for recurrent networks and small batches?
hypothesis: Fixing the mean and variance of the summed inputs within each layer reduces covariate shift and stabilises hidden-state dynamics in RNNs without batch dependence.
contributions: Layer normalization: mean and variance over all hidden units in a layer on one training case, with per-neuron gain and bias, identical at train and test time
Invariance analysis against batch and weight normalization (Table 1)
Geometry-of-parameter-space analysis using the Fisher information of normalized GLMs
Experiments on six tasks, mostly RNNs

method.summary: Layer norm replaces batch statistics with per-case statistics over the H hidden units of a layer, then applies learned gain and bias before the non-linearity. It is inserted into LSTM/GRU recurrences in existing Theano codebases and compared with the unmodified models and with batch norm on six tasks.
method.task: Training-speed and generalisation comparison of normalization schemes across image-sentence ranking, reading comprehension, skip-thought sentence embeddings, DRAW on MNIST, handwriting generation, permutation-invariant MNIST

results.quote: layer normalization is invariant to scaling of the entire weight matrix and invariant to a shift to all of the incoming weights in the weight matrix

code.snippet: mu^l = (1/H) sum_i a_i^l ; sigma^l = sqrt((1/H) sum_i (a_i^l - mu^l)^2)
LN(z; alpha, beta) = (z - mu)/sigma * alpha + beta
LSTM gates = LN(W_h h_{t-1}; a1,b1) + LN(W_x x_t; a2,b2) + b ; h_t = sigma(o_t) * tanh(LN(c_t; a3,b3))
